samples.name: @tanstack/solid-start-server
evidence: All 18 archive members inspected; no appended payload, links, optional git dependencies, or install lifecycle scripts.
A fresh exact-version registry fetch has identical SHA-256 5e25dd250ebee8a27d6b17f50a2bf2a4c7ea2aa109ec478ea5181e53d0c28f1f.

Entry point exports SSR adapters and start-server-core; defineHandlerCallback is an identity function. Adapters forward app-provided router/request/headers to Solid renderToString/renderToStream and return HTML Responses.
All three sourcesContent fields equal the shipped TypeScript source.

Direct runtime dependencies and the solid-js peer minimum fetched and inspected; no malicious execution chain found. Ancillary exact developer versions and internal context/stub dependencies also fetched.
The README Scarf URL returns a 68-byte PNG and represents a document analytics pixel, not executable payload. The notable URL detection is retained.
Upstream advisory names solid-start-server 1.166.54 and 1.166.57, not this 1.166.51. A broad package/incident label or confusion with react-start-client 1.166.51 could explain malware categorization.
changes: Relocated a name-only source-map trait from a VS Code bundler branch to the file-extension subject, preserving matcher, type/platform scope, confidence and criticality.

limitations: No deployment context, lockfile, or authenticated publisher intent was supplied.
Range dependencies were examined at the named lower version, and wildcard Vite at the current fetched 8.3.5; these are not proof of a historical resolved dependency tree.
No native disassembler is applicable to these plain JavaScript/TypeScript npm archives. Static call paths and complete archive contents establish their supported behaviors.

The installed atomscan embeds an older validator; CLEAVE_VALIDATE was unset for atomscan while all focused rule checks and final validation use the newer source-matched Cleave binary. Atomscan also reports model feature-spec v18 versus extractor v19.

consumer_policy.direct_references: Preserved; a source-map path remains available to explicit map-context exclusions.
consumer_policy.ancestor_directory_references: Audited. A source-map filename does not establish a bundle, minifier helpers, or benign build-tool output. Do not add it back into general build-directory selectors. The narrowing corrects that unsupported inference, not an observed attack behavior.

regression.source_map_cases: Baseline trait confirmed MATCHED via test-rules; normal scan output can strip it.
regression.baseline_output_filtering: The original source-map path and three canvas filename/assignment baselines remain matching, but the engine may omit low-tier facts when unrelated notable findings are present. Canonical notable source-map filename and format detections remain.
regression.unsupported_context_narrowing: Map filenames no longer imply VS Code/bundler output through metadata/build ancestry.

comparison_options: atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none --format json; original HEAD rules in scratch compared with edited working rules, same exact sample paths and registry map.
remaining_disagreements: The two Aikido malware-list labels disagree with the supported benign behaviors. Their exact labeling rationale is unavailable.
No final classifier/verdict disagreement; all three remain classifier BENIGN.
material_detection_losses: None in attack coverage. Three unchanged canvas baseline rules still match in test-rules but are filtered from emitted output after the new drawing notables. Source-map capability/name coverage and direct source-map exclusions remain; general bundler provenance must no longer be inferred from a filename.
